title: MegaPX: Fast and Space-Efficient Peptide Assignment Method
author: Lutfi, Ahmad

steps.title: Set up computational environment
steps.instruction: Install Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS 64‑bit on a machine with standard GPU configuration, then install Casanovo and SMSNet. Load the pre‑trained Casanovo weights from the original publication and the SMSNet model from Beslic et al. 2023. Make the HCD library from MassIVE (1,114,503 annotated peptides) available for both models.

steps.title: Run de novo sequencing models
steps.instruction: Execute Casanovo on the MS/MS spectra, then run SMSNet using the published de novo pipeline. Use a precursor tolerance of 10 ppm and a fragment mass tolerance of 0.02 Da. Set carbamidomethylation of cysteine as a fixed modification and oxidation of methionine plus deamidation of asparagine and glutamine as variable modifications.

steps.title: Filter peptide predictions by confidence
steps.instruction: For each predicted peptide, calculate the peptide‑level confidence as the average of its amino‑acid‑level confidence scores. Apply a default confidence threshold of 70 % for routine analyses. In mutation‑rich contexts, relax the threshold to 50 % to increase recall of variant peptides while still discarding most low‑confidence predictions.

steps.title: Prepare reference bins for indexing
steps.instruction: Load the user‑defined reference protein sequences into memory and split them into batches according to the user‑defined M split size. Remove outlier references using an optional blacklist file before further processing.

steps.title: Generate k‑mers and mutational variants
steps.instruction: K‑merize each reference sequence to the chosen length k. If mutation generation is enabled (boolean 1), create mutational variants for each k‑mer using the BLOSUM62 substitution matrix, keeping only substitutions with a similarity score above the user‑defined threshold and stopping early when scores fall below that threshold. Encode all (original and mutated) k‑mers as 64‑bit integers and, optionally, compute minimizers on the forward strand only.

steps.title: Build Interleaved Bloom Filter (IBF)
steps.instruction: Set the target false positive rate to 0.01. For each bin, determine maxKmers (the maximum number of k‑mers any bin can contain) and size the Bloom filter accordingly. Use three hash functions H to hash the encoded k‑mers, insert the hashes into their respective Bloom filters, and interleave the equal‑size filters into a single IBF (total size = b × n, where b is the sub‑bit vector size and n the filter length).

steps.title: Query peptides and construct count matrix
steps.instruction: K‑merize each de novo peptide to the same length k and query its k‑mers against the IBF. Record the number of k‑mer hits per bin to build count matrix C (rows = peptides, columns = user bins).

steps.title: Compute assignment thresholds and scores
steps.instruction: Choose a user‑defined assignment threshold D (percentage). For each peptide, compute x = y × D / 100, where y is the total number of k‑mers in that peptide. Build a binary lookup matrix (1 = hit, 0 = miss) based on whether the peptide meets the threshold in each bin. Calculate the assignment score S for each bin using the provided lookup‑table formula.

steps.title: Assign taxonomy and output results
steps.instruction: Use the assignment scores to map each peptide to the corresponding user bin (protein or species). Generate the final report containing peptide‑to‑protein matches, taxonomy assignments, and any relevant scoring metrics.
